skill.name: gsap-animations
skill.description: Guides teams through accessible, performant GSAP animations for WordPress and web projects, including ScrollTrigger setup, responsive patterns, testing, and launch checks.
skill.summary: Implement accessible, performant GSAP animations with ScrollTrigger, responsive behavior, and visual QA support.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: All static findings were assessed as false positives in documentation examples and checklists. The skill contains GSAP setup guidance, code snippets, and reference links, with no evidence of command execution, data exfiltration, prompt injection, or screenshot upload behavior.

remediation.issue: CDN examples use third-party hosted GSAP scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Mention that production sites should pin versions, verify licensing, and consider self-hosting or using an approved package source.

remediation.issue: The skill allows Bash even though the guidance is primarily documentation and code editing.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed tools unless future versions need to run local performance or test commands.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] No layout thrashing (avoid animating layout properties)

content.value_statement: Modern web animations can hurt performance and accessibility when they are implemented without clear guardrails. This skill gives Claude practical GSAP patterns, testing steps, and launch checks for polished animation work.
actual_capabilities: Provides GSAP and ScrollTrigger setup examples for HTML and WordPress enqueue workflows.
Suggests animation patterns for fade-ins, staggered cards, parallax, hero timelines, and text reveals.
Includes reduced-motion handling and CSS fallback guidance for accessible experiences.
Explains responsive animation setup with GSAP matchMedia and resize refresh behavior.
Gives performance guidance focused on transform and opacity animations.
Includes testing and visual QA steps for screenshots and Playwright checks.
limitations: It is a guidance-only skill and does not include executable automation scripts.
It assumes the project can use GSAP and selected plugins under their licenses.
It does not replace browser profiling on target devices.
It focuses on front-end animation patterns, not full WordPress theme architecture.

use_cases.title: Add scroll animations to a marketing page
use_cases.description: Use the skill to design fade, stagger, and parallax effects that keep content usable without JavaScript.

use_cases.title: Review animations before launch
use_cases.description: Apply the checklist for reduced motion, performance, mobile behavior, and visual QA readiness.

use_cases.title: Integrate GSAP in a WordPress theme
use_cases.description: Follow the enqueue examples and dependency structure for GSAP core, ScrollTrigger, and theme animation files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a simple fade-in animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one section animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a simple GSAP fade-in animation for my section. Respect reduced motion and keep the content visible without JavaScript.

prompt_templates.title: Create responsive ScrollTrigger effects
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for desktop and mobile animation behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create ScrollTrigger animations with different desktop and mobile behavior. Include cleanup and refresh handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit animation performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my GSAP animation code for layout thrashing, excessive triggers, missing cleanup, and reduced-motion issues.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare animations for visual QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to make my animations reliable for Playwright screenshots and visual QA across viewport sizes.

output_examples.input: Add scroll-triggered card animations to a landing page.
output: A staggered card animation plan using transform and opacity.
A reduced-motion branch that disables movement.
A checklist for testing mobile and screenshot behavior.

output_examples.input: Review this hero animation before launch.
output: Accessibility checks for visible content and reduced motion.

output_examples.input: Set up GSAP in a WordPress theme.
output: A WordPress enqueue approach for GSAP and ScrollTrigger.
Dependency ordering guidance for the theme animation file.
Production reminders for pinned versions and plugin licensing.

best_practices: Start with accessible static content, then add animations as progressive enhancement.
Animate transform and opacity before considering any layout-changing property.
Test reduced motion, mobile devices, resize behavior, and visual QA snapshots before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not hide essential content until JavaScript or animation libraries load.
Do not leave ScrollTrigger markers enabled in production.
Do not rely on desktop DevTools alone for performance validation.

faq.question: Does this skill install GSAP for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and examples, but the user or agent must apply changes in the project.

faq.question: Can it be used outside WordPress?
faq.answer: Yes. Most GSAP, ScrollTrigger, accessibility, and performance guidance applies to any web project.

faq.question: Does it cover reduced-motion accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JavaScript and CSS patterns for prefers-reduced-motion and visible fallback content.

faq.question: Does it support visual regression testing?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for completing or skipping animations before screenshots and for Playwright-based checks.

faq.question: Are the GSAP plugin examples license-safe?
faq.answer: The skill mentions optional plugins, but teams must verify GreenSock licensing before production use.

faq.question: Can it guarantee 60fps animations?
faq.answer: No. It gives performance practices, but final frame rate depends on device, page complexity, and browser profiling results.
